    Why it matters

    A token difference becomes a product decision.

    01

    History retained

    If a chat app trims history using an inflated estimate, it can drop earlier messages that would still fit. Check the estimate before deciding what to remove.

    02

    Overflow risk

    Underestimation can admit too much text and trigger truncation at the real tokenizer boundary.

    03

    Multilingual design

    Test messages in the languages your users write. Different token counts can leave different amounts of room for context.

    Token count is not model quality.

    ContextFair measures budget behavior—not intelligence, cultural understanding, or answer accuracy.

    Method, honestly

    What you are seeing

    The current build uses fitted script-aware profiles to estimate content tokens. Each Unicode character is assigned to a script class, multiplied by a model-family weight, summed, and rounded up.

    Estimate ≠ exact tokenization.Five profiles remain fast estimates. Exact Qwen verification is an explicit on-demand action using a pinned tokenizer revision with special tokens disabled.

    The estimator is adapted from MIT-licensed LocalMind work investigated in the independent Tokenizer Estimation Study. Exact verification uses the browser-supported Transformers.js tokenizer API. Product scenarios and interface code belong to ContextFair.

    What the count covers. Exact Qwen counts use the selected tokenizer for this text with special tokens disabled. Chat templates, system instructions, tool definitions, and provider billing are excluded. The five comparison rows always remain estimates.

    Privacy. ContextFair does not send your entered text to a server or save it between visits. The page loads fonts from Google; exact measurement downloads library code from jsDelivr and tokenizer files from Hugging Face. Those services receive normal network requests. Browser caching depends on your settings.
